newsitem.title: THAILAND: Alphatec delays new share issue, swaps.
newsitem.headline: Alphatec delays new share issue, swaps.

text.p: Thai semiconductor company Alphatec Electronics Plc said on Friday it has delayed its plan to float shares in the United States and to buy shares of electronic firms.
The company said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand it would postpone its plan indefinitely.
The suspension of the share issue was partly due to the low level of the Thai bourse, the company said.
Alphatec said last month it planned to raise its registered capital to 803 million baht ($30.88 million) from 414 million baht by issuing 38.9 million new shares.
Of the new shares, 25 million would have been offered to foreign investors through an issue of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
The remaining 13.9 million shares would have been be issued to swap for shares of NS Electronics Bangkok (1993) Co Ltd and Alphasource Manufacturing Solutions Plc.
Alphatec also said loan negotiations between creditors and its majority-owned Submicron Technology Co Ltd had not yet been completed.
As a result Alphatec said it would postpone its investment in Submicron.

Alphatec said last month it would spend two billion baht from its share issue to buy 167 million shares of Submicron. After the purchase, Alphatec's holding in Submicron would rise to 46.87 percent from 2.5 percent.
The major shareholder and founder of Submicron is Charn Uswachoke, who is also Alphatec's chief executive and major shareholder.
